textbook: Clean cutaway textbook illustration of a SINGLE human endothelial progenitor cell (EPC), a flattened, elongated, migrating animal cell, centered in a square 1:1 1080x1080 frame with lots of negative space around structures for later labels. Fill the whole square edge-to-edge on a neutral dark charcoal background with NO border, frame, vignette or letterbox. Match the exact house look of a refined educational plate: a MUTED, slightly desaturated palette (soft dusty tints, never bright primary or cartoon colours), THIN clean outlines (not heavy black strokes), gentle soft shading, each structure its own distinct soft colour fill. The cell is fan/spindle-shaped, wider and rounder at the trailing end and flattening into a broad, thin, CONTINUOUS, solid sheet-like leading lamellipodium (like a smooth webbed paddle or fan blade with a gently scalloped but essentially unbroken outer edge), about 2 to 3 times longer than wide overall. Paint the lamellipodium with the SAME warm pale tan/peach cytoplasm colour fill as the rest of the cell body (just as a soft, even, flat colour wash, continuous with the main cell colour) — it must NOT be left plain grey or a different cool colour from the rest of the cell. At most 3 to 5 short, stubby, irregularly-spaced filopodia may poke out unevenly from the lamellipodium's outer edge. A neat quarter cut-away reveals the interior: a single ovoid nucleus set toward the trailing half containing one prominent nucleolus, pale cytoplasm, folded rough endoplasmic reticulum sheets studded with tiny ribosome dots near the nucleus, a curved stack of Golgi apparatus cisternae, several small oval mitochondria with faint inner cristae scattered through the cytoplasm, fine actin filaments concentrated at the cell cortex and running as stress fibres toward the leading edge, and a handful of distinctive elongated ROD-SHAPED Weibel-Palade secretory granules (clearly longer than wide, cigar-shaped, NOT round) scattered in the cytoplasm near the Golgi. Anatomically faithful animal cell. Do NOT draw a cell wall, nucleoid, plasmids, chloroplasts, a large central vacuole, or round platelet-style granules; this is NOT a bacterium, NOT a round red blood cell, and NOT a platelet. CRITICALLY: do NOT draw a dense uniform comb/fringe of many thin radiating hair-like spikes around the cell margin — that reads as motile CILIA on a ciliate protozoan (like Paramecium), which is WRONG for this human cell; the leading edge must look like a solid membrane sheet, not a hairbrush. Absolutely NO text, letters, numbers, labels, scale bars, arrows, or watermarks in the image.
